title: Corner: 30-Minute Live Demo Script
summary: Beat-by-beat script for Patrik's live demo calls. Exact words, exact screen moments, exact questions to ask. This is how Corner gets sold.
content:
Corner: 30-Minute Live Demo Script

For: Patrik (runs every sales demo with this) Prerequisite: 15-minute discovery call already happened. You know their industry and top pain point. Setup: Screen share Patrik's actual Corner instance (NOT a staging environment. The real thing with real AOM data.) Duration: 25-30 minutes

PRE-CALL PREP (5 min before)

Pull up Corner in a clean browser tab. Confirm:

  • Logged in, office loaded
  • Checklist view visible (not game view — start calm, reveal the game later)
  • At least 3 tasks visible: one Right Now, one To Do, one Completed
  • Agent chat is accessible
  • You know the prospect's name, business name, and the #1 thing they said ate their time

MINUTE 0-2: OPENING

(Don't share your screen yet. Just talk.)

"Thanks for taking the time. Before I show you anything — just want to make sure I'm showing you the right thing. Last time we talked you mentioned [THEIR PAIN POINT]. Is that still the #1 thing?"

Let them answer. This is a human moment. Listen.

"Perfect. So everything I show you today, I want you to think about it through that lens: would this have handled [THEIR PAIN POINT]? If the answer's yes, we've got something. If not, I want to know."

"Ready to see it?"

MINUTE 2-5: THE CHECKLIST (The Calm Open)

(Share screen. Start in Checklist view.)

"This is Corner. I want to start simple — this is the Checklist view. Think of it as the clean, fast version. Everything your team is working on, organized."

Show the Right Now column.

"'Right Now' is what's actively happening. Not what's queued. What's actually being worked on at this exact moment."

Hover over a task.

"Every task is owned by an agent. This one's owned by [AGENT NAME]. It knows what the task is, who it's going to, and what to do with it when it's done."

Click a task to expand it.

"You can see exactly what the agent has on it: the context, the output it's working toward, the status. Nothing is a black box."

Pause.

"Does this feel familiar? This is basically a team task board — except the people doing the tasks don't need managing."

MINUTE 5-10: AGENT CHAT (The Human Moment)

(Navigate to the chat interface.)

"Here's where it gets real. I want to show you something."

Type a message to an agent. Something specific to their industry.

For Construction: "Hey [Scheduler] — add a task to follow up with Johnson Electric about Tuesday's estimate."

For CPA: "Hey [Client Manager] — draft a reminder email for clients who haven't submitted Q1 docs yet."

For Agency: "Hey [Outreach] — pull together a list of open leads that haven't heard from us in 10+ days."

Watch the response come in.

"That just happened. I typed it like a text message. The agent understood it, confirmed it, and it's now in the task queue."

Point at the task appearing in the checklist.

"There it is. Without me clicking anything. Without filling out a form. I told my team what I needed. They're on it."

Pause and let them react.

"When's the last time that's what a new task looked like?"

MINUTE 10-15: THE GAME (The Jaw Drop)

"Okay. I want to show you something that looks different than any software you've seen. This is why Corner doesn't feel like software."

(Switch to Game view.)

Let them see it for 3-5 seconds before saying anything. Let the silence do the work.

"This is the same data. Same agents. Same tasks. Just... alive."

Pan slowly across the office.

"Each room is an agent. Right now you can see [AGENT 1] is working — their room is lit up, there's activity. [AGENT 2] is between tasks — their room is quieter. It's not a decoration. This reflects real system state."

Point at a room with activity.

"If I click this room, I'm opening a direct line to that agent. Same chat we just used."

Click a room, open chat.

"And I can see everything they've done — their completed tasks, their recent output, their current status."

Zoom out.

"Most of my clients react to this one of two ways. Either 'this is the coolest thing I've ever seen for business software' — or 'this is interesting but I want the clean checklist.' Both are valid. You get both. Toggle between them anytime."

Ask: "What's your gut reaction?"

(Listen. Adjust the rest of the demo based on their answer. If they love the game, stay here longer. If they want functional, go back to checklist.)

MINUTE 15-20: YOUR BUSINESS VERSION

"I want to show you what this would look like for [BUSINESS NAME]."

(If the custom demo page exists: navigate to it with their business pre-populated. If not: describe it verbally while showing AOM's instance.)

"Based on what you told me, here's the team I'd build for you:"

Walk through the 6 agents from the one-pager template:

"1. Operations — routes everything, gives you the morning briefing. 2. Scheduler — owns your calendar, sends you prep notes before every meeting. 3. Follow-Up — [SPECIFIC TO THEIR PAIN POINT. Example: 'This is the one that handles the thing you said was your #1 problem — client follow-up. Every lead gets a response. Same day. Your agent never lets one fall through.'] 4. [INDUSTRY-SPECIFIC AGENT] 5. Content — drafts your social posts, project updates, client communications. 6. QA — reviews what every other agent does before it comes to you. Nothing goes out unchecked."

Pause.

"With this team, what specifically would change about [THEIR PAIN POINT]?"

(Let them answer. This is where they sell themselves.)

MINUTE 20-23: THE MORNING CHECK-IN ROUTINE

"Let me show you what your Monday morning would look like."

(Return to the checklist view.)

"It's 7am. You open Corner. Here's what you see:"

Walk through it like it's their morning:

"'Right Now' shows two things already in flight — agents started these before you woke up. [TASK 1 relevant to their industry]. [TASK 2 relevant to their industry]."

"'Completed' — these are from overnight. [TASK relevant to their pain point] is already done. You don't have to do it. You just have to review and approve."

"The whole check-in takes 10 minutes. You approve what looks good. You redirect anything that's off. And you go do the work that only you can do."

"The rest is handled."

Beat.

"What does your Monday morning look like right now?"

(Let them paint the contrast.)

MINUTE 23-27: OBJECTIONS (BE READY FOR THESE)

"How do I know the agents won't make mistakes?" "QA agent reviews everything before it reaches you. You're always the approver. Nothing goes to a client without you seeing it. Think of it as a team where everyone's work gets reviewed before it ships. That's how it works."

"Is this like ChatGPT?" "ChatGPT answers one question and forgets you exist when you close the tab. These agents know your business. They know your clients by name, your projects by status, your preferences from every conversation you've had with them. ChatGPT doesn't know what's in your calendar. These do."

"What if I want to change something?" "You just tell them. Literally type it. 'Stop scheduling meetings on Friday afternoons.' Done. Or if it's a bigger change — adding a new agent, retraining one — that's a 30-minute call with us. Included in your plan."

"$3,500/month seems like a lot." "Let me flip that. What's your time worth per hour? If you're billing at $150/hour, and this saves you 10 hours a week — that's $6,000/month in recovered time. You're paying $3,500 to get $6,000 back. And that's before the leads you don't lose anymore."

(Alternatively: "Compare it to what you'd pay one person. A part-time office manager is $30-40k a year. A marketing person is more. For $42k a year, you get six people who never call in sick, never quit, and work 24/7. The math only makes sense one way.")

"Can I try before I pay?" "Yes. Two ways. One: the demo page at aheadofmarket.com/demo — fully interactive, no sign-up. Two: we offer a 30-day money-back guarantee. If Corner doesn't save you measurable time in the first 30 days, I'll refund your first month. No negotiation, no hard feelings."

MINUTE 27-30: THE CLOSE

(Don't sell. Summarize and let them decide.)

"Here's where I'll leave it:"

"You told me [THEIR PAIN POINT] is costing you [TIME/MONEY they mentioned]. We just walked through exactly how Corner handles that — [SPECIFIC AGENT] takes that off your plate. The team would be live in 48 hours."

"Three options from here:"

"One: you're ready to move forward. Reply 'I'm in' to the email I send you, and we'll have your office set up by [DAY]."

"Two: you want to think it over. I'll send you the one-pager today — that covers everything we discussed plus exact pricing and next steps. No pressure."

"Three: you have more questions. Happy to do a second call. I'd rather answer everything before you commit than have you wonder."

"What makes sense for you?"

(Stop talking. Let them answer.)

POST-CALL ACTIONS (within 24 hours)

  • Send one-pager PDF (fill in corner-one-pager.md template)
  • Send follow-up email (from corner-one-pager.md template)
  • Log the call in your prospect tracker (business name, date, tier interested in, next step, follow-up date)
  • If they said "I'm in" — send the agreement + Stripe link same day

IMPORTANT RULES FOR THE DEMO

Use real data. AOM's real Corner instance, real tasks, real agents. Not a fake demo environment. When they see "Follow up with Johnson Electric" in your task list, they believe it works. Mockups don't convert. Reality does.

Don't rush the game reveal. Let the silence sit after you switch to game view. Let them stare. Their reaction tells you everything about how to close them.

Don't list features. Every feature you show should be in the context of their specific pain. "Here's the feature" = eyes glaze. "Here's how this solves the thing you mentioned" = they lean forward.

Ask questions. The demo is a conversation, not a presentation. At every major moment: "Does this feel familiar?" / "What's your gut reaction?" / "What does that look like for you right now?" They sell themselves.

If something breaks: "One of the things I love about showing you the real product — it means I sometimes have to explain what I'm seeing live. This is [WHAT'S HAPPENING]. It doesn't affect [THE VALUE YOU WERE SHOWING]. Let me keep going."

Never panic. Real product demos have friction. That friction proves it's real.
